title: Balanced Binary Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- recursion call stack: up to h deep (worst case skewed tree h = n → O(n); balanced tree h = log n)
- no containers or arrays allocated
- not counted: input tree
approach: A tree is height-balanced when, for every node, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most 1. A post-order DFS computes each subtree's height exactly once: it returns the height if the subtree is balanced, or -1 as a sentinel if it is not. As soon as any child returns -1 or the height gap exceeds 1, the call short-circuits and propagates -1 upward, so every node is visited at most once.
hints: If you compute the height of each node's subtrees independently from scratch, how many times does the deepest leaf get visited across all those computations?
Post-order DFS: each call returns the subtree height, or -1 to signal imbalance. In Example 1, node 20's children 15 and 7 each return height 1, so 20 returns 2.

```
function check(node):
    if node is null: return 0
    left = check(node.left)
    if left == -1: return -1
    right = check(node.right)
    if right == -1: return -1
    if |left - right| > 1: return -1
    return max(left, right) + 1

return check(root) != -1
```

**Empty tree** - root is null
`Input: []` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: accessing root->left without a null check → crashes

**Single child** - one child only, height difference of 1 is allowed
`Input: [1,2]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using `abs(left - right) >= 1` as the imbalance test instead of `> 1` → returns false

**Skewed tree** - linked-list shape, imbalance detected deep inside
`Input: [1,2,null,3,null,4]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: not checking whether a child returned -1 before computing `abs(left - right)` → returns true

**Balanced at root, imbalanced in a subtree** - root's subtrees have equal heights but one contains an imbalance
`Input: [1,2,3,4,5,null,6,7,null,null,null,null,8]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: only checking balance at the root node → returns true

followUps.q: What if the balance threshold is k instead of 1?
followUps.a: Replace `abs(left - right) > 1` with `abs(left - right) > k` in the same DFS. The sentinel and short-circuit logic stay identical. TC O(n), SC O(h).

followUps.q: What if you also need to verify the tree is a valid BST (i.e., check if it is an AVL tree)?
followUps.a: Extend the DFS to carry (minAllowed, maxAllowed) bounds. At each node, check val is within bounds, then recurse left with (minAllowed, val) and right with (val, maxAllowed). Return height or -1 as before. TC O(n), SC O(h).

followUps.q: What if the tree has 10^7 nodes and recursion may overflow the call stack?
followUps.a: Convert to an iterative post-order traversal using an explicit stack with a visited flag per node. Push node then its children; on second visit compute height from children's stored results. TC O(n), SC O(h) with an explicit stack instead of the system call stack.
